keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «어떤 동물은 스스로 빛을 만들 수 있고, 이것을 생물 발광이라고 한다(주제)» 와 «빛은 많은 생물에게 강력한 생존 도구다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (some animals can make their own light, which is called bioluminescence) and the conclusion (light is a powerful survival tool for many living things). The green sentences are the answers.

sum.pre: Some living things can make their own
, and this is called bioluminescence. It happens when special
inside their bodies mix. Fireflies use their glow to find
on summer nights. The anglerfish uses a glowing lamp on its head to
small fish, and some squid release glowing clouds to confuse their
. Light is a powerful survival tool for many living things.

words: special chemicals inside their bodies mix and give off light
substances that can mix and change into something new
happening often or found in many places
on its head to attract small fish
a powerful survival tool for many living things

qs.q: Why is glowing far more common in the deep sea?
qs.qko: 깊은 바다에서는 왜 빛을 내는 생물이 훨씬 흔한가요?
opts: Because the water there is warm
Because many boats shine lights there
evs: But in the deep sea, where sunlight never reaches, glowing is far more common.
These lights do not come from boats or cameras.
Unlike a light bulb, this light makes almost no heat.
Scientists use the chemicals behind this glow as tools in medical research.
why: 햇빛이 전혀 닿지 않는 깊은 바다에서 빛을 내는 일이 훨씬 흔하다고 했어요. 배나 카메라의 불빛은 이 빛과 관계가 없어요.
Glowing is far more common in the deep sea, where sunlight never reaches. The lights do not come from boats or cameras.

qs.q: In “glowing is far more common,” what does “common” mean?
qs.qko: «glowing is far more common» 에서 «common» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: In fact, most animals that live in the deep ocean can make light.
Some mushrooms on land can glow as well.
These lights do not come from boats or cameras.
Scientists use the chemicals behind this glow as tools in medical research.
why: 다음 문장에서 «깊은 바다에 사는 동물 대부분이 빛을 낼 수 있다» 고 했어요. 대부분이 그렇다면 «흔한», 곧 자주 볼 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
The next sentence says most animals in the deep ocean can make light. If most of them can, glowing is «common», or happening often.

qs.q: How does the anglerfish use its light to catch food?
qs.qko: 아귀(anglerfish)는 빛을 이용해 어떻게 먹이를 잡나요?
opts: Its glowing lamp draws small fish close, and then it quickly swallows them
It shines its light into their eyes so they cannot swim
It releases glowing clouds to trap small fish
evs: The anglerfish has a glowing "lamp" on its head to attract small fish.
When curious fish swim closer, the anglerfish quickly swallows them.
Some squid even release glowing clouds to confuse enemies and escape.
But in the deep sea, where sunlight never reaches, glowing is far more common.
why: 아귀는 머리에 달린 빛나는 «등불» 로 작은 물고기를 끌어들이고, 궁금해서 가까이 온 물고기를 재빨리 삼켜요. 빛나는 구름을 뿜는 것은 오징어예요.
The anglerfish uses its glowing lamp to attract small fish, and when they swim closer, it quickly swallows them. Squid are the ones that release glowing clouds.

ends: How do fireflies talk with their flashing lights?
What other strange animals live in the deep sea?
깊은 바다에는 또 어떤 신기한 동물이 살까?

write.src: “Let’s <u>look for fireflies tonight</u> before <u>the summer ends</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «함께 할 일 + 그보다 나중에 일어날 일» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what we should do together and what happens after that.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «before» 뒤에 «무엇이 + 어떻게 되는지» 를 넣어 때를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: before the lights go out)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «before», write what + what happens to make the time clear. (e.g. before the lights go out)
